Subject: Packaging options for upcoming renewal

Hi Lukas,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We reviewed the usage graphs and want to explore a sensible upgrade path ahead of our Oct renewal. A few constraints on our side:
- We need predictable per-token spending for chat generation (peak windows matter).
- Embeddings volume will increase next quarter (~10k/month vectors).
- Procurement prefers consolidated invoices rather than add-on line items.

Can you send a short options summary that shows:
1) A conservative upgrade (minimal price uplift) that addresses token spikes,
2) A recommended bundle that reduces unit cost for embeddings, and
3) Any trade-offs (e.g., higher latency risk with aggressive quantization).

If you could also include procurement-friendly language (SLA, invoice cadence, early-termination credits), that would help.

Best,
Sasha
Sasha Patel
Head of AI Product, Shelfline
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Packaging options for upcoming renewal

Thanks Sasha — attaching a concise package comparison (shelfline_pricing_v2.xlsx) and a one-page upgrade summary (shelfline_upgrade_summary.pdf). High level below:

Options (summary):
- Option A — Predictable Boost (entry upgrade):
  - Move to Dedicated Lite pool (reserved baseline capacity)
  - 10% uplift on current spend, 20% headroom for spikes
  - Token SLOs: 95% requests < 180ms (generation)
  - Pros: Minimal CAPEX commitment; simple per-month invoice
  - Cons: Slightly higher per-embedding unit cost

- Option B — Embedding Saver (recommended if embeddings grow):
  - Dedicated Standard + Embedding precommit (monthly vector block)
  - ~18% uplift but reduces embedding unit price by ~35% at 10k vectors/month
  - Includes monthly usage report and a 30-day regression guard for prompt quality

- Option C — Performance-Max (for sustained high throughput):
  - Dedicated High concurrency, custom kernel optimizations, optional quantized model variant
  - 30%+ uplift, best per-token economics on sustained load
  - Trade-offs: quantized variants may add 5-10ms to median latency in worst-case tails

Procurement notes included in the attachments: invoice cadence options (monthly/quarterly), SLA language, and suggested termination credit for the reserved component.

Next steps: if you want, I can create a one-column recommendation for your procurement team showing annualized TCO for Option A vs B. Marissa — looping you for approval on a limited promotional discount we can apply for the first 3 months (Shelfline is in our mid-market expansion bucket).

Thanks,
Lukas

Subject: Re: Packaging options for upcoming renewal -- technical knobs

Adding technical context for the bundle trade-offs Sasha called out:
- Embedding Saver (Option B): we pre-allocate an embedding cache and batching window. That improves cost per vector but requires ~2x memory headroom on the Dedicated node. If Shelfline's embedding growth is bursty, we'll recommend a small autoscale buffer to avoid degraded tail latencies.
- Quantization: good for Token cost reduction (esp. for batched completion workloads) but avoid for sensitive generation where hallucination risk matters.

I'll draft a short paragraph for the one-pager on the measurable QA checks we apply post-migration (prompt set regression, sample-based BLEU-style checks, and live user SLO monitoring).

—Aditya
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
